characters.maya: A logged-in shopper who opens the Ember stove at 100% rollout. Her request is the one traced in Acts 2-3.

beats.label: Monday, 09:00
beats.title: Baodium wants a “Recommended for you” row on every product page.
beats.body_md:
Recommendation Service already powers the **home page** and **checkout**. Reusing it is four lines of code. The unit test passes. Code review approves.

Look at the store on the right: shoppers browse, and every page loads quickly.

beats.label: 09:02 · 1% of customers
beats.title: It ships behind a feature flag, to 1% of customers.
beats.body_md: A feature flag lets the team turn the row on for a small group first. Nothing changes on the dashboards.

beats.label: 09:06 → 09:13 · 25%, then 50%
beats.title: 25%. Then 50%. The median page doesn't move.
beats.body_md: The slowest pages get a little slower, but still well under the 300 ms objective. Nobody is paged.

beats.title: Everyone gets the row. Pages crawl.
beats.body_md:
Watch the shoppers: their pages take seconds. Home-page and checkout recommendations are slow too, though nobody touched them.

Follow **Maya**, highlighted, as she opens the Ember stove.

beats.label: X-ray
beats.title: Same moment, seen from the inside.
beats.body_md:
Each figure is now a request. Product Page asks Catalog (fast), then calls Recommendation Service, which must **borrow one of 40 database connections** before its query can run.

All 40 are busy. Everyone else waits in line. That amber line is the incident.

beats.label: X-ray · Maya's request
beats.title: Where did Maya's time go?
beats.body_md:
The timeline under the picture splits one real request into its parts. The **SQL itself** is quick. Almost all of the time was spent **waiting for a connection**.

The database isn't slow. The queue in front of it is. The chapter calls these intervals **acquisition**, **execution** and **occupancy**.

beats.label: Act on it
beats.title: Turn the flag off, and time how long recovery takes.
beats.body_md:
Doubling the pool or adding instances would spend more of PostgreSQL's **shared** session budget, which checkout also depends on. Turning off the optional feature removes the demand.

[button: Turn personalization off]

_It won't be instant: 8 Product Page instances refresh the flag every 15 seconds, one by one._

beats.label: What you saw
beats.title: Three things to carry into the rest of the book.
beats.body_md:
**1. Acquisition is not execution.** Requests waited for a connection while the SQL stayed fast. Query metrics alone would have said “database fine.”

**2. Exposure is not traffic.** “1% of customers” said nothing about how many lookups reached one pool of 40.

**3. Optional work must stay optional.** In the chapter's fix, the page gives recommendations at most 150 ms and a limited number of permits, then renders without them.
